traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Droseraceae: leaves usually alternate, rarely whorled; leaves usually simple, rarely compound; stipules present or absent; leaf rosettes usually none, often basal; plants hermaphrodite; ovary superior; floral cup present or absent; stems herbaceous; flowers solitary or in cymes; flowers actinomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit capsule; parts of each whorl 4 to 5; stamens (4-) 5 to 20; carpels 3 (-5). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.vernation.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 378, family Droseraceae: vernation circinate or folded; read as "circinate".

traits.flowering_position.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 378, family Droseraceae: flowering position terminal; read as "terminal".
